summary: An interior page (p.5) of The Anaconda Standard for Tuesday, September 17, 1895, mixing local crime and accident reporting with commercial advertising. The page is dominated visually by a large D.J. Hennessy Mercantile Co. blanket-sale advertisement occupying the entire right third of the page. The left and centre columns carry three substantial news stories — a bank-robbery conviction, a fatal accident involving a child, and miscellaneous local items — alongside column advertisements for clothing, jewellery, wines, and dental and furniture businesses. The editorial tone is matter-of-fact and typical of a regional daily, with sensational headlines balanced by dense text columns.
headlines: THE FRIGHTFUL DEATH OF A LITTLE TW AND A HALF-YEAR-OLD GIRL

clipping_placements.placement_note: top of col 2, directly adjacent to the 'HORRIBLE ACCIDENT' lead story; shares upper page with it but yields visual priority to that larger headline

juxtapositions: The 'HUDSON WAS GUILTY' bank-robbery conviction story sits immediately beside the 'HORRIBLE ACCIDENT' child-death story at the top of the page, pairing urban crime with domestic tragedy in the same visual band.

The dense crime and accident reporting in the left and centre columns runs hard against a full-column Hennessy's blanket-sale advertisement on the right — the same Hennessy's store whose witness helped convict Hudson in the adjacent trial story.
